summary: Three bighorn sheep hunters above 13,000 ft near Missouri Mountain; the successful shooter developed severe altitude sickness (repeated vomiting, blood-tinged) after butchering the kill; the party dropped into Iowa Gulch toward their truck and called 911. Three Chaffee County SAR South members hiked from the Missouri Gulch trailhead with oxygen while a helicopter with the team doctor circled for hours unable to land near the subjects (it eventually landed on Missouri Ridge ~13,000 ft and the doctor descended on foot). Ground team rendezvoused with the party near 11,000 ft after dark, administered oxygen, and assisted the four-hour nighttime descent, fording a knee-high river around midnight to the road and a waiting ambulance where EMTs treated the sick subject. No serious injuries.
location: Iowa Gulch / Missouri Gulch, Missouri Mountain
notes: Date inferred: author's own site dates the write-up 2022-09-14 ('last week' mission); 2022 CO bighorn sheep rifle season opened Sept 6 (Day 1), mission the next morning, finished ~midnight Sept 7/8. One patient with altitude sickness (oxygen, EMT treatment), two companions assisted in descent. Story by CCSAR South member Cameron Torres.
